draft.title: A primitive conversion fails when nested inside a traced broadcast
draft.body:
## Reproducer

Run this example

```julia
using Reactant
f(x) = sum(Float64.(x[1:3]) .+ log.(1:3))
x = Float32[1, 2, 3]
compiled = Reactant.@jit f(Reactant.to_rarray(x))
@assert compiled ≈ f(x)
```

## Observed

On Reactant 0.2.289 the nested broadcast fails during element-type inference. The standalone conversion succeeds.

## Expected

The compiled reduction should match Julia and preserve the element conversion when used inside another broadcast.

## Proposed fix

Construct the unary primitive-conversion broadcast node with the traced TypeCast before nesting it. This keeps fusion and gives inference a callable that accepts traced scalars. The fork implementation is proposed in [PR #3360](https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Reactant.jl/pull/3360).

problems.title: Traced branches capture indexing begin and end as variables
problems.summary: An indexing endpoint in a traced branch or condition can raise UndefVarError before the branch runs. The local macro filters the indexing symbols; the original report records the fix in ExpressionExplorer 1.1.6.

fix.why_together: One commit changes capture filtering and includes the condition/branch regression matrix.

problems.title: Gathering linear indices from a traced adjoint or transpose fails
problems.summary: An index vector into a traced row wrapper can raise BoundsError during compilation. Materializing the wrapper before gathering preserves order and conjugation; normalization must also preserve index shape and static bounds checks.

commits.title: Fix linear indexing of traced adjoint and transpose wrappers
Preserve static index validation and gather shape

fix.why_together: The first commit handles wrappers and the second retains Boolean masks, invalid-index errors and Cartesian result shape.
